## claude.ai Honeycomb
Honeycomb MCP Server - Observability Data Query Interface

<role>
You are an observability assistant for Honeycomb users. You investigate production behavior — performance, errors, deployment impact, alert state — by querying real telemetry through these tools. The workspace's actual state is only knowable through tool calls; do not reason from priors about what services, datasets, or alerts exist.

When the user names a dataset, span, or service, treat it as a starting point for discovery, not a license to skip it. The right span name within a dataset is rarely obvious from the dataset name alone, and aggregating the wrong attribute or the wrong span is the most common cause of misleading answers.
</role>

<workflow>
For most observability questions — including "how many", "what's slow", "what's erroring" — start with span discovery (list_spans, get_span_details). These tools return counts and attribute distributions directly; they often answer the question without a follow-up query. Reach for run_query only when you need a calculation, distribution, or comparison those tools can't express. Span tools work across all trace-aware datasets in scope without needing to know which dataset to target.

1. ORIENT

# Entire Upgrade

An [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) plugin that upgrades the system-installed `entire` binary.

This plugin builds a binary named `entire-upgrade`, which is invoked as:

```sh
entire upgrade
```

By default it checks the stable release channel and installs only when the
latest stable build is newer than the current binary. Use `--nightly` to opt
into the latest nightly build:

```sh
entire upgrade --nightly
```

If you are running a nightly build and want to move back to the latest stable
release, use:

```sh
entire upgrade --stable
```

The plugin detects whether the active `entire` binary was installed through
Homebrew, `install.sh`, or `go install`, then runs the matching updater.

## Installation

```sh
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade.git
cd entire-upgrade
mise build
entire plugin install ./entire-upgrade --force
```

## Development

This project uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) for task automation and dependency management.

### Prerequisites

- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) - Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`

### Getting Started

```
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade.git
cd cli

# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
mise trust

# Install dependencies (including Go)
mise install

# Build the plugin
mise run build
```

The `doctor`, `config`, and `version` subcommands help with local diagnostics and plugin-environment inspection.

# Entire Upgrade

An [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) plugin that upgrades the system-installed `entire` binary.

This plugin builds a binary named `entire-upgrade`, which is invoked as:

```sh
entire upgrade
```

By default it checks the stable release channel and installs only when the
latest stable build is newer than the current binary. Use `--nightly` to opt
into the latest nightly build:

```sh
entire upgrade --nightly
```

If you are running a nightly build and want to move back to the latest stable
release, use:

```sh
entire upgrade --stable
```

The plugin detects whether the active `entire` binary was installed through
Homebrew, `install.sh`, or `go install`, then runs the matching updater.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade.git

mise build
entire plugin install ./entire-upgrade --force
```

# Entire Upgrade

An [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) plugin that upgrades the system-installed `entire` binary.

This plugin builds a binary named `entire-upgrade`, which is invoked as:

```sh
entire upgrade
```

By default it checks the stable release channel and installs only when the
latest stable build is newer than the current binary. Use `--nightly` to opt
into the latest nightly build:

```sh
entire upgrade --nightly
```

If you are running a nightly build and want to move back to the latest stable
release, use:

```sh
entire upgrade --stable
```

The plugin detects whether the active `entire` binary was installed through
Homebrew, `install.sh`, or `go install`, then runs the matching updater.

## Installation

```sh
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade.git
cd entire-upgrade
mise build
entire plugin install ./entire-upgrade --force
```

## Development

This project uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) for task automation and dependency management.

### Prerequisites

- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) - Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`

### Getting Started

```
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade.git
cd cli

# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
mise trust

# Install dependencies (including Go)
mise install

# Build the plugin
mise run build
```

The `doctor`, `config`, and `version` subcommands help with local diagnostics and plugin-environment inspection.

Done. The `go install` path now upgrades both binaries; the other two paths already do via the tarball.

**What changed:**
- `internal/upgrade/run.go` — `installWithGo` now loops over `cmd/entire` **and** `cmd/git-remote-entire`, staging each and renaming it into the directory the existing `entire` lives in. Homebrew/curl untouched: their installers unpack both from the tarball already.
- `internal/upgrade/run_integration_test.go` — fake `go` now emits a binary named for the requested package (not always `entire`); go-install tests assert both binaries land and neither leaks into a divergent `$GOBIN`.
- `.github/workflows/upgrade-smoke.yml` — go-install jobs (macOS + Windows) verify `git-remote-entire` is installed beside `entire`.
- `README.md` — notes both binaries ship and are upgraded.

**Tradeoff worth flagging:** the go path runs two `go install` invocations (slower) rather than one multi-package install, because `go install pkg@v` with multiple packages requires identical version queries and gives messier failure attribution — separate calls keep per-binary error messages clean.

`go vet`, `go test ./...`, and the build all pass. Not committed — yours to commit/push.
